subsystems.name: Extraction units
subsystems.role: gather raw material from regolith, asteroid rubble or a moon's surface.

subsystems.name: Materials refinery
subsystems.role: turn rock and metal into usable feedstock.

subsystems.name: Deposition heads
subsystems.role: fuse or weld material into structure without a factory.

subsystems.name: Mobile printer swarm
subsystems.role: thousands of machines crawling over the growing structure.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: supply the enormous energy the process needs.

subsystems.name: Control network
subsystems.role: keep the swarm coordinated over continent-scale distances.

subsystems.name: Product structure
subsystems.role: the megastructure itself, printed in place.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Sample the target rock or asteroid and measure what it contains, so the process chemistry can be fixed.

buildSteps.title: Anchor a pilot plant
buildSteps.detail: Land a machine that mines, refines and prints a single small structure — a beam, a panel or a landing pad a few metres across.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate closed-loop printing
buildSteps.detail: Prove the plant can mine, process and print a part with no material shipped from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Prove self-replication
buildSteps.detail: The decisive step: have the plant build a working copy of itself. Growth is exponential only if this succeeds.

buildSteps.title: Scale into a swarm
buildSteps.detail: Copies make copies; the population doubles every cycle until it numbers thousands or millions of units.

buildSteps.title: Build the seed structure
buildSteps.detail: The swarm prints a small version of the target — a ring segment, a collector panel array — and tests it against micrometeoroids, thermal cycling and radiation.

buildSteps.title: Deposit at scale
buildSteps.detail: Units crawl or fly along the growing surface, adding material continuously; the structure extends by kilometres per day in principle.

buildSteps.title: Operate and renew
buildSteps.detail: The same swarm repairs, replaces and expands the structure for decades rather than being discarded.

prerequisites.why: turning local rock into oxygen, water and metal has been demonstrated in labs and in small space experiments but not at industrial scale.

prerequisites.tech: Additive manufacturing in vacuum and microgravity
prerequisites.why: polymer printing is routine on the space station and metal printing has been tested there, but nothing close to structural beams is proven.

prerequisites.tech: Regolith and metal sintering or melting
prerequisites.why: concentrated-solar and microwave sintering of simulated lunar soil works in laboratories; it has not run on the Moon.
swarms of tens of robots are demonstrated on Earth; millions of units coordinating across thousands of kilometres is not.
exponential growth, the whole point of the concept, requires machines that can build complete copies of themselves — nobody has shown this even partially.
reusable rockets have cut launch cost sharply, but seeding a swarm still needs orders of magnitude more mass delivered.

pathway.milestone: laboratory sintering of simulated regolith and small robotic construction experiments
pathway.unlocks: proof that local material can be turned into solid structure.

pathway.milestone: a robotic plant on the Moon or an asteroid that mines, refines and prints one usable object

pathway.unlocks: exponential growth — the only route to planet-scale output.

pathway.milestone: swarm construction of a 40,000 km orbital ring around Earth, or the first collector panels of a stellar swarm
pathway.unlocks: structures whose scale is set by material supply rather than by launch capacity.

pathway.milestone: a swarm of collectors capturing a meaningful fraction of the Sun's 3.8×10²⁶ W output, needing hundreds of billions of square kilometres of surface
pathway.unlocks: civilisation-scale energy, if the physics of stability, repair and heat rejection can be solved.
